The backup folder is where Manual Save stores your save slots.

If the game crashes or is killed while a save was in progress, the Watcher detects the abandoned session and turns it into a recovery backup.
Crashes are detected automatically. You don't need to do anything to enable this.
When the game starts cleanly, the Watcher checks for sessions that never closed. Any orphaned save folder is copied to a new slot named with a _crash_<timestamp> suffix.
Your original save is never deleted by this process.
On the next main menu after a crash, a popup lists the recovered slots so you can find them in the Load screen.
Treat them like any other manual save. Load to inspect, rename to keep, delete once you've confirmed everything is fine.
They may contain partial world state if the crash happened mid-save. Don't blindly overwrite a good slot with one without checking.

WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU CLICK QUICK SAVE

On a 500ms loop it does four things:
1. Reads small .txt signal files from Zomboid/Lua/.
2. Copies, moves, or deletes folders in Zomboid/
   using robocopy.
3. Runs PowerShell to capture the game window.
4. Writes a Done file back so the game sees the result.

A manual save is a folder copy. Lua inside PZ
cannot do that. The Watcher is the smallest
possible workaround: an external Windows process.

HOW IT TALKS TO THE GAME

The Watcher polls %USERPROFILE%\\Zomboid\\Lua\\
for ManualSave_Signal.txt written by the Lua side.
Parses the op > runs it > writes Done.txt back.

game can detect if the Watcher process dies.
